title: Checkachagin
summary: An Oyster Bay waterway name preserved through place-name research, with an approximate Beaver Lake/Mill Neck marker rather than a traced brook line.
address_label: Beaver Swamp Creek / Beaver Lake area, Mill Neck, NY (approximate)
why_this_matters: Checkachagin preserves a personal-name placename for an Oyster Bay brook flowing toward Beaver Swamp Creek, with records connecting it to Chechagon or Quaropin. The modern marker is approximate rather than a traced brook line, but the name still links a waterway to a remembered Native person and local community geography. Brook names can carry human history, not only descriptions of land and water.
introduction_content: Checkachagin is a brook name from Oyster Bay, recorded by Tooker as flowing northeasterly into Beaver Swamp Creek. Later and local forms include Chaugren, Chogorin, and Choggin.
translation_content:
Checkachagin is treated as a personal-name placename rather than a translated landscape description. The recorded forms connect the brook with Chechagon or Quaropin and with later spellings Chaugren, Chogorin, and Choggin.

Why Place Names Matter

“There are many names which conjoin historical and physical information.”

— Isaac Taylor, Words and Places (1873), Internet Archive scan leaf 50
whereintheworld_content: Checkachagin keeps a brook, a Native person named in deed records, and local memory tied together in the Oyster Bay landscape. The approximate marker makes the waterway visible while leaving room for a future traced creek line.
